question.text: During the reign of this emperor, the siege of the Masada ended the First Jewish Revolt. This emperor is said to have fiddled during the Great Fire of Rome.
question.clue: This leader's mother Agrippina the Younger was initially his regent, but he eventually had her assassinated.

swap.leadin: A period of expansion into Germany under this ruler was ended by defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
swap.text: Name this first Emperor of Rome, who conquered Egypt through victory at the Battle of Actium.
swap.answerHtml: Octavian [or Augustus Caesar or Gaius Octavius; do not accept or prompt on just “Caesar”]
swap.clue: The Second Triumvirate consisted of Antony, Lepidus, and this adopted son of Julius Caesar, who fought a civil war against Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BCE and became the first Emperor of Rome.

question.text: With Cleopatra, this triumvir commanded the losing army at Actium. This man killed himself thinking that Cleopatra was dead, which led to her suicide.
question.clue: Cicero's head and hands were sent to this leader after Cicero attacked him in his writings and this man was defeated at the Battle of Actium.

swap.text: This large Roman arena built by Vespasian and Titus was often used for gladiatorial games or mock sea battles, the "circuses" in Juvenal's quote.
swap.clue: The Colossus of Nero was located near this building, whose hypogeum is an underground network of tunnels and cages used to house slaves.

question.leadin: This leader led a force of allied tribes which were ultimately defeated at the Battle of Watling Street.
question.text: Name this leader of the Iceni people who destroyed Camulodunum while leading a revolt following the death of Prasutagus.
question.clue: This leader's first target was Camulondunum, which was burned to the ground after the defeat of the Ninth Legion.

swap.leadin: This civilization's capital of Veii ("VAY-ee") was sacked by the forces of Marcus Furius Camillus, and was legendarily led by king Lars Porsenna.
swap.text: Name this ancient Italian civilization that was assimilated into the Roman republic.
swap.answerHtml: Etruscans (“eh-TRUSS-kuhnz”) [or Rasenna; or Rasna; or Tusci; or Etrusci; or Turrhenoi; or Tursenoi; prompt on Tyrrheni or Tyrrhenians]
swap.clue: According to Livy, these people created a group whose leaders were chosen at the Fanum Voltumnae in Volsinii every year.

question.leadin: Caracalla is presented by many sources as a tyrant, but he wasn't all bad.
question.text: One of Caracalla's great public projects was the construction of his namesake one of the these things, the second-largest in Rome. These places were fed water by aqueducts which was then heated by log fires.
question.clue: Slaves called unctores would often use a strigil on their masters in the destrictarium of these places.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Roman infrastructure.
swap.text: More than 400,000 km of these structures helped link the Roman Empire together. Spartacus and his followers were crucified along one of these structures.
swap.clue: One of these structures was called "Salaria" for its role in the salt trade.

question.text: Tarquinius Superbus fled to this king of Clusium, whose campaign to reinstall the king was foiled by the determination of Mucius Scaevola.
question.clue: This figure was saved from death when a would-be assassin mistook his scribe for him, and that assassin thrust his right hand into a fire in an act of defiance against this figure.

swap.text: Roman emperors tended to live on this hill, which was the location of Nero's Golden House and the Domus Tiberiana.
swap.clue: Dionysius of Halicarnassus places the home of one individual near the Scalae Caci on the south side of this location.

question.leadin: Identify these things related to the early days of Rome.
question.text: The revolt that resulted in Tarquinius' deposition was sparked by his son's rape of this woman.
question.clue: After that, a man threatened to place the naked corpse of a slave next to this woman's bed to frame her for adultery.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the early years of the Byzantine empire.
swap.text: Two advisors to Constantine had this name. The one from Caesarea wrote histories like the Chronicon.
swap.clue: The man who baptized Constantine had this name. A more famous Roman with this name was a Bishop of Caesarea who wrote an Ecclesiastical History of the early church.

question.text: As part of his reunification of the Roman Empire, Aurelian was forced to abandon this Roman province north of the Danube, which had been established by Trajan after conquering a namesake tribe under King Decebalus.
question.answerHtml: Dacia [or Roman Dacia or Dacia Traiana or Dacia Felix; accept Dacians]
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.text: Early in his revolt, Spartacus's followers hid out at this location. At a battle on this place, the slaves used vines to grapple down a cliff and defeat Claudius Glaber's army.
swap.clue: Artifacts excavated from towns next to this feature were confined to a Secret Museum due to their incredibly erotic content.

question.text: Part of the Catiline Conspiracy's downfall was sealed when letters about the conspiracy sent to the Allobroges (AHL-oh-BROH-gayz), a tribe from this Roman province, were intercepted at the Milvian Bridge.

swap.leadin: In 2023, Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, and Brent Seales organized a crowdsourced attempt to do this task, for which the Diamond Light Source particle accelerator was used.
swap.text: Name or describe this task. To achieve this task, virtual unrolling and AI-based segmentation were used on objects from Naples.
swap.answerHtml: reading papyrus [or deciphering the Herculaneum papyri; or reading the scrolls from the Villa of the Papyri; or Vesuvius Challenge]
swap.clue: The city of Pergamon is credited with developing vellum as an alternative to this substance.

question.leadin: The front side of the Samnian Table of Agnone described ceremonies to be held in its sanctuary dedicated to an analogue of this Roman goddess of the grain at modern-day Pietrabbondante.
question.text: What lead goddess of the Plebeian Triad names an Aventine hill temple with Liber and Libera and is the Roman counterpart to Demeter?

swap.text: An earlier defeat of Pompey was to this man who set up an independent little state in Spain. This man also brought the pain to Metellus and made Pompey cry back to Rome for help. This man was finally killed by some of his pompous henchmen.
swap.clue: Along with his lieutenant Hirtuleius, he overthrew the governor Quintus Metellus Pius, and then was joined by Marcus Perpenna, though Perpenna eventually had this man murdered at a banquet.

question.text: The First Punic War was sparked by this group of Italian mercenaries, who requested Carthaginian aid after losing to Hieron II, but switched to the Roman side when the Carthaginian army arrived.
question.clue: Pyrrhus was also opposed by this band of mercenaries hired by Agathocles, the Tyrant of Syracuse. They later sided with Rome against Syracuse and Carthage during the First Punic War.

swap.leadin: Many garum factories, like the one at Baelo Claudia, were located in this region.
swap.text: Name this region which at various points during Roman rule contained the provinces of Baetica, Lusitania, Tarraconensis, and Citerior. The Visigoths conquered most of this region during the 5th century.
swap.clue: Quintus Sertorius fought a namesake guerilla campaign in this region, which was finally conquered by Augustus in 19 BC. This home to the Cantabrians was originally divided into "Ulterior" and "Citerior" portions by the Romans.
